primary_sources.title: Mazur and Mottola, Weyl Cohomology and the Effective Action for Conformal Anomalies
primary_sources.reviewed: Section IV, especially the conformal Ricci identity (38), Paneitz operator (40), Wess-Zumino functional (44), local trace identity (46), and finite R-squared convention (54)-(56), opened directly.
primary_sources.use: Standard local conformal and trace identities. Its discarded surface terms do not specify this problem's boundary action. The actual coefficients and domain are inherited from the retained model.

source_access: The primary paper and relevant passages were opened directly; no downloaded-byte digest is claimed.
strongest_comparator: The preceding finite-cut action calculation supplies an algebraic second-order conformal cancellation but expressly leaves its field-equation compatibility unproved. General anomaly theory supplies the trace; it does not compare these forced nonlinear boundary tails in the retained action.
hardest_step: Keep the nonlinear density contact and vacuum shift, derive the quadratic trace forcing independently from physical curvature invariants, and compare the forced trace and action tails before interpreting any cancellation as a solution.
new_consequence: Within the explicit second-order expansion, the trace-compatible conformal tail has a remaining normalized cutoff cosine coefficient strictly below -3/56 for every t>0. The action-cancelling tail has a strictly nonzero trace residual. The conformal-only repair is therefore insufficient; the necessary coupled shape relation is derived without adopting it as a solution.
scope: Fixed background cut and stated conormal expansion. The full shape equation, its canonical determinant and boundary variation, static compatibility, causal response and exact nonlinear existence remain open.
exploratory_work: Before source freeze, exact symbolic explorations derived the leading Euler row and independently recovered it from warped-metric curvature invariants. They are development calculations, not acceptance runs.
verification_scope: Exact action/curvature derivations and matrix incompatibility; refined charged static trace fixtures and independent complex-amplitude Taylor extraction. Fixed nonzero-frequency transfer uses an ordinary radial power count.
